claims.statement: EMA's Clinical Trials Information System supports sponsor-authority interactions across the trial lifecycle and makes public searchable information available, including sponsor, recruitment dates, trial dates, and locations subject to transparency rules.

CTIS public information must balance transparency with protection of personal data and commercially confidential information, so any private outcome layer requires separate permissions and careful disclosure controls.
Hypothesis: independent sites will contribute verified operational metrics to earn a portable reliability credential, and CROs will pay when it improves feasibility decisions beyond public CTIS data.

contrary_evidence: CROs and sponsors already maintain private preferred-site histories and may treat them as strategically confidential.
Public CTIS records do not provide all site-level operational outcomes needed for a fair score.

economics.acquisition_route: Hypothesis: launch free CTIS-derived Polish site profiles, let sites verify public facts, then sell one therapeutic-area feasibility pack to a CRO.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 5 buyers and 50 sites in year 2, 35 buyers and 400 sites in year 4, and 120 European buyers at 50000 PLN average annual revenue in year 7 yields 6M PLN ARR before site tools. At 4-6x ARR and 50-65% ownership, founder equity can exceed 5M PLN if independent outcome contributions become durable.
economics.founder_time: Hypothesis: 15-22 hours/week through the first paid feasibility cycles, with medical and governance review contracted.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 70-82% after data verification, site appeals, security, and analyst support.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 9-18 months at 30000-70000 PLN enterprise acquisition cost and 50000-120000 PLN first-year buyer value.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 30000-80000 PLN/year per CRO or sponsor team plus 500-1500 PLN/month site workflow tier that does not affect ranking.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Hypothesis: every study repeats site selection; operational histories and portfolio integrations support annual buyer renewal above 85%.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Longitudinal site-level startup, recruitment, data-quality, and closeout outcomes with transparent normalization and appeals
fingerprint.customer: Independent Polish clinical-trial sites seeking differentiation and CRO/sponsor feasibility teams selecting sites
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Free verified site profiles, CTIS-linked discovery, site networks, and CRO feasibility workflow integrations
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Public-data site map, permissioned operational benchmark, portable site credential, and contributor-gated feasibility intelligence
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: CRO/sponsor pays for search and decision support; site optionally pays for workflow tools but never for a higher score
fingerprint.problem_trigger: New-country feasibility, site shortlist, study startup, or annual preferred-site review

founder_fit: Neuroscience and medical adjacency support understanding of study workflows.
Data-quality, uncertainty, and fair benchmarking are core data-science problems.
Public CTIS data enables a product demonstration without outreach or private records.
A self-serve site profile and contribution workflow can reduce founder networking load.
risks: A flawed score could unfairly damage site reputation; transparent methodology, minimum samples, appeals, and no pay-to-rank are essential.
Commercially confidential and patient information must never leak into benchmark outputs.
Chicken-and-egg adoption between sites and CRO buyers.

structure.control_point: fair, permissioned site reliability history used in feasibility selection
structure.critical_dependency: trusted two-sided contribution with defensible attribution and confidentiality

thesis: A contributor-gated feasibility and reliability index for independent Polish clinical-trial sites. It combines public CTIS facts with permissioned operational outcomes such as startup time, recruitment delivery, query burden, and closeout reliability, giving sites a fair credential and CROs a better repeat-selection tool.
title: TrialSite Reliability Exchange for Poland
uncertainties: Sites and CROs may disagree on metric definitions, attribution, and appeal rights.
The sales cycle and information-security bar may be difficult alongside full-time employment.
The 75000 PLN capital estimate and all numeric business assumptions below are planning hypotheses.
